inz4ouQ6C5k.text: Why don't magnets lose their power? Think about it. A magnet can attract things for years without ever needing to be recharged. So why doesn't it run out? Because a permanent magnet isn't constantly using energy to stay magnetic. Inside it are tiny regions called magnetic domains. In a strong magnet, many of these domains stay aligned in the same direction, creating its magnetic field. And that arrangement is stable. So a magnet doesn't simply run out like a battery. ours_A1_female.first_3s: Your fingers wrinkle in the bath, but your elbows don't.
ours_A1_female.text: Your fingers wrinkle in the bath, but your elbows don't. Why? For years, we thought skin just soaked up water like a sponge. But here's the twist. If the nerves in a finger are cut, it never wrinkles at all. So wrinkling is your body's choice. Tiny blood vessels squeeze, and the skin folds into grooves. Those grooves push water away, like the tread on a tire. Wet things are easier to grip. So next time you're in the bath, try picking up a wet marble. Which hand wins?

hZIw8_M-5Ww.first_3s: Why do some people feel they need a cigarette
hZIw8_M-5Ww.text: Why do some people feel they need a cigarette to poop? It starts with nicotine, which reaches your gut through your blood. There, it activates gut nerves that release acetylcholine. That chemical tells your colon to squeeze, and things start moving. Over time, your body ties smoking to the toilet, making it acute. But your gut adapts, and without nicotine, things can slow to a crawl. That's why quitting can cause constipation for a few weeks. But nicotine isn't a healthy laxative. Long term, it raises the risk of ulcers, reflux and colon polyps. Coffee, exercise and fiber can get things moving
